accounting.rationale: J3/24-007 PDF 46, printed 32, lines 2-4: three descriptive-text conventions. The defining section is Text conventions, not a general rule classifying every note or example in the standard.
Equivalent ordinary English wording can stand for a syntax term in descriptive prose. Requirements therefore cannot be found by matching italic grammar names alone.

Upper-case keywords identify particular statements and attributes in the prose, with END as the source's example. This typographic convention does not require upper-case letters in a Fortran source program; 6.1.2 governs case equivalence.

Descriptions of obsolescent features use smaller type. This supplies a source-review cue, not an executable feature or a waiver of support. The real, qualified reporting-capability obligation is retained under 4.2 p2(2)/S4.2-002. 4.4.3 p2 (PDF 52) cross-references this typography.

PDF 46, local note between lines 4 and 5: demonstrates the smaller type size. The demonstration is not itself a Fortran feature. This source-only disposition covers this note alone; notes, examples, annexes and obsolescent features elsewhere still need their own source accounting and review.

review_rationale: Independent source-first review and tested integration repairs: doc/source_audits/batch_006.json. The local explanatory/informative conventions are classified without turning notes or examples into additional mandatory requirements.
